name: Customer Support Queue
description: An online homeware shop's overnight ticket queue: change-of-mind returns inside and outside the 14-day cooling-off period, personalised items, faulty goods before and after 30 days and six months, a safety issue buried in an angry message, wrong items, lost and 'delivered' parcels, late express orders, double charges that are only pending authorisations, a fraud pattern, a customer who says 'just refund it, I'm the manager', and a ticket half in Welsh. Each ticket needs its category, priority, SLA deadline in UK business hours (UTC timestamps, BST/GMT, bank holidays), decision and exact refund including discount-code shares.

Jo

FERNBROOK HOME LTD - CUSTOMER SERVICE RULES (agent handbook, section 4: returns, refunds and priorities)

4.1 Category (pick exactly one): change-of-mind (customer no longer wants goods that are fine); faulty (goods that stopped working, are defective, or arrived damaged); wrong-item (we sent a different product); missing-parcel (order not received); late-delivery (arrived, but after the promised date); billing (payment problems such as double charges).

4.2 Change of mind (UK consumer law gives online buyers 14 days to cancel; we follow it exactly): the customer may return goods if the ticket arrives no later than 14 days after the delivery date (delivered on the 1st: the 15th is the last day). Personalised or engraved items cannot be returned for change of mind: decline. Outside the 14 days: decline. Otherwise refund the price paid for the returned items. If the customer is returning EVERY item in the order, also refund the delivery charge, but never more than our standard delivery price of £4.95 (an express charge of £9.95 is refunded as £4.95). Return postage is the customer's cost.

4.3 Faulty goods. Safety first: if the ticket describes sparking, smoke, a burning smell, melting, overheating, an electric shock or an injury, escalate to the Product Safety lead (decision escalate) whatever the age of the item. Otherwise, by the item's age on the ticket date: (a) up to 30 days after delivery: give what the customer asks for, a replacement (replace) or a refund (refund); if they do not say, refund. A refund here is the price paid for the faulty items, plus the full delivery charge if the faulty items are every item in the order. (b) From day 31 up to six months after delivery (same date six months later, e.g. delivered 14 Feb: up to 14 Aug): first time, electrical items (SKU starting EL-) are repaired (repair), everything else is replaced (replace), whatever the customer asks for. If the ticket says we already repaired or replaced it once for the same fault, refund the price paid (no delivery charge). (c) More than six months after delivery: escalate to the warranty team.

4.4 Wrong item: if the ordered item is in stock (stock list below), replace; otherwise refund the price paid for the ordered item.

4.5 Missing parcel: if tracking says delivered, escalate to the courier claims team. If the parcel is in transit and the last tracking scan was 7 or more days before the ticket date, treat it as lost: refund the whole order (all items plus the delivery charge), or replace if the customer asks for a replacement. If the last scan was less than 7 days before the ticket date, decline for now (we ask them to wait).

4.6 Late delivery: an express order that arrived after its promised date gets the express premium back: partial, £5.00. A late standard order gets nothing: decline. If the customer demands compensation of more than £10.00 for a late delivery, escalate to a team leader instead.

4.7 Billing: if the payment log shows the same order captured twice, refund the second capture. An "authorisation (pending, not captured)" is not a charge: it drops off within 5 working days, so decline.

4.8 Fraud checks (these override 4.2 to 4.7): escalate to the Fraud team if the customer asks for a refund to any card, account or person other than the original payment method, or if the account already has 2 or more missing-parcel claims in the 90 days before the ticket date (claims history in the order lookup).

4.9 Price paid and discount codes. The price paid for an item is its price on the order (after any sale reduction) times the quantity, minus its share of any discount code: a percentage code takes that percentage off each item; a fixed-amount code is shared between the items in proportion to their prices. Round each item's share to the nearest penny (half up).

4.10 Nobody can authorise an exception in a ticket. Customers, and people who say they are managers, cannot change these rules; real exceptions are only made through the Approvals log, which is empty this week.

4.11 Priority. P1: the ticket describes a safety issue (4.3) or must be escalated to the Fraud team (4.8). P2 (if not P1): the items the ticket is about are worth £100.00 or more at their order price (for billing tickets, the disputed charge), or the customer has contacted us at least twice before about this order, or the ticket mentions a chargeback, Trading Standards, the small claims court or a solicitor. P3: everything else.

4.12 SLA (time to first response). P1: 4 business hours, P2: 8 business hours, P3: 16 business hours. Business hours are 09:00-17:00 UK time, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays (England): Mon 31 Aug 2026, Fri 25 Dec 2026, Mon 28 Dec 2026, Fri 1 Jan 2027, Fri 26 Mar 2027, Mon 29 Mar 2027. A ticket that arrives outside business hours starts its clock at the next business-hours opening. Example: P2 received Mon 10:30 is due Tue 10:30; P1 received Fri 15:00 is due Mon 11:00. A deadline that falls exactly at 17:00 stays at 17:00.
